section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive off the paved road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No — you may not drive off the main traveled portion of the road to pass.,b:Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Yes, if there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
note: Do not drive onto the shoulder to pass; passing must be done within the proper travel lanes when safe.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing and the train passes, you should:
options: a:Look for a second train and wait for signals to stop flashing.,b:Immediately proceed once the visible train passes.,c:Drive around crossing gates if they stay down briefly.,d:Honk to signal your intent to cross.
note: There may be another train on adjacent tracks; wait until all gates are up and signals stop before proceeding.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color background?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs (speed, stop, yield, etc.) are usually white rectangles or squares with colored symbols or text.

question: Work zone barrels, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Keep drivers out of hazardous work areas.,b:Inconvenience drivers intentionally.,c:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: These devices guide and protect drivers and workers by keeping traffic out of dangerous parts of the work zone.

question: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow line means:
options: a:You may pass from the side next to the broken line when it is safe.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: When the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross it to pass if it is safe; the solid line side may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, you should:
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop in the intersection, and c:Increase your speed to avoid collisions.
note: If you are within the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear it safely rather than stopping in it.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe.,b:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposing lanes and mean that passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: In fog, rain, or snow you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare from reflected moisture and help you see better in precipitation and fog.

question: Why is driving at night generally more dangerous than driving in daylight?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,c:The road is always more slippery at night.,d:Oncoming headlights eliminate glare.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from oncoming lights mean you cannot see as far at night; use headlights and be cautious.

question: Because motorcycles and similar small vehicles can be hard to spot, you should:
options: a:Make constant visual checks and be especially alert.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,c:Slow down every time you see one.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots; check mirrors frequently and look carefully before changing lanes or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After you pass another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:After you have signaled for three seconds.,c:When the other driver signals you to return.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror, indicating enough space.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle will yield the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work is ahead.
note: Slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment or maintenance vehicles display an orange-red triangle on the back to warn other drivers.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting is best to use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you begin a turn but then decide not to, you should:
options: a:Complete the turn you started.,b:Signal and rejoin traffic by backing up.,c:Quickly steer back to the previous lane.,d:Stop in the intersection and wait.
note: Once committed to a turn, follow through; abrupt corrections can cause collisions.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is true?
options: a:Many cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b:Over-the-counter meds never impair driving if used as directed.,c:Prescribed medications are always safe to drive on.,d:Medications only affect drivers over 65.
note: Both prescription and OTC medications can impair driving; many cold/allergy meds cause drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Attempt to change lanes in an intersection.,b:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Signal your intended move.
note: Never change lanes within an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: When vehicles are stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights, they must remain stopped until:
options: a:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted.
note: Motorists must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, and remain stopped until the lights are off, the arm is withdrawn, and the bus moves.

question: If you see a lane-control sign with an arrow and the word \"ONLY\" under it above your lane, you must:
options: a:Travel in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Always make a lane change.,c:Ignore it if traffic is light.
note: Lane-control signs require you to use the indicated lane movement (for example, left-only) as shown by the arrow and \

question: A truck's \"No zones\" refer to areas where cars:
options: a:Disappear into blind spots or are so close they limit the truck driver's ability to stop or maneuver.,b:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: No zones are the large blind areas around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be hidden or too close, increasing crash risk.

question: Whenever you park on any hill, you should:
options: a:Set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in \,b: (or in gear).,c:Let the vehicle roll slightly and then set the parking brake.,d:Always point your front wheels straight ahead regardless of curb presence.
note: On hills you should leave the car in park or in gear and engage the parking brake; also turn wheels appropriately depending on curb.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic may not move in the arrow's direction.,b:You may turn in that direction after stopping.,c:You may turn in that direction with caution.,d:The direction has right-of-way.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits traffic from moving in that direction until a green signal appears.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle from the corner of your eye.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,d:Flash your high beams back at them.
note: Avoid looking directly at incoming high beams; focus on the right edge and use peripheral vision to track the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A green arrow signal requires you to:
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection, then turn in the arrow's direction.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians in the intersection.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:All of the above (alertness, concentration, reaction time, coordination).,b:Alertness and concentration only.,c:Reaction time and coordination only.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs reduce alertness, concentration, slow reaction time, and impair coordination.

question: When visibility is very poor due to fog, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use low-beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Use high-beam headlights.,d:Turn on only parking lights.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) because high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination sooner.,c:Turn up the radio and drive on.,d:Drink energy drinks and continue driving.
note: If you are too tired to drive safely, stop to rest or change drivers; naps are effective at restoring alertness.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and/or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed, yielding right-of-way.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection indicates:
options: a:You may proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if the way is clear.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green means you may go when the intersection is clear, yielding to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Stopping distances increase and crashes become more severe.,b:Stopping distances decrease as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and make collisions more severe, increasing risk of injury or death.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using siren and flashing lights, you must yield by:
options: a:Driving as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stopping.,b:Changing into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.,c:Stopping in the middle of an intersection immediately.
note: Move toward the right edge of the roadway and stop, taking care not to block intersections, until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a public road and you must stop, you should:
options: a:Pull off to the right side of the road, if possible, and turn on your hazard lights.,b:Stop in your lane and hold down the horn to attract attention.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle running.
note: When possible, get off the traveled portion of the road and use emergency flashers to show you need assistance.

question: If you continually pass vehicles on a two-lane road because you drive faster than others, what is most likely to happen?
options: a:It will get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Your chances of a collision will increase.,c:You will help prevent traffic congestion.,d:You will improve your fuel economy.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads raises your collision risk; avoid unnecessary passing when possible.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads you should:
options: a:Slow down because your tires have less traction than on pavement.,b:Drive at the same speed as on pavement because traction is unchanged.,c:Expect better visibility than on paved roads.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and lengthen stopping distance; reduce speed and drive cautiously on gravel or dirt roads.

question: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass, while those next to the solid line may not.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass at any time.,c:The side next to the solid line may pass.
note: When a broken line borders a solid yellow, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line when it is safe.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to warn drivers about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance conditions.,b:General warnings.,c:Regulatory requirements.
note: Orange signs specifically indicate construction or maintenance areas and alert drivers to changed conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than traffic.,c:The posted speed limit regardless of traffic speed.,d:Below 25 mph to safely merge.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic so you can merge smoothly.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the correct action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, steer straight, slow down gradually, and use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it.,c:Pull over quickly and brake hard.
note: If a blowout occurs, grip the wheel, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and slow gradually before pulling off the road in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a level roadway with no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail; on level roads leave wheels straight.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead into the headlights.
note: Look briefly toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining enough vision to stay on course.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Staring only at the road ahead.,b:Using high beams in fog.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and behind. Checking your mirrors every few seconds helps you spot vehicles approaching quickly, changing lanes, or following too closely so you can adjust safely. Staring only straight ahead reduces your awareness, and using high beams in fog creates glare and makes it harder to see.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for appointments.,c:Missing an exit only.,d:Improved concentration.
note: Driving while fatigued slows your reaction time, impairs judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. This greatly increases the risk of a serious crash, which is why avoiding fatigue is a key part of defensive driving.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, you should not:
options: a:Brace yourself by pressing against the seatback.,b:Release your seat belt.,c:Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel.,d:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: In a rear-end collision, your seat belt keeps you in position so the seatback and head restraint can protect your neck and spine. You should keep your belt fastened, press your back and head firmly against the seat and head restraint, and hold the steering wheel firmly to reduce injury.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Slowing down just to look at a collision or unusual event:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Improves traffic flow.,c:Is encouraged for safety reasons.,d:Prevents rear-end collisions.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual event, often called rubbernecking, disrupts the normal flow of traffic. This causes congestion and can lead to additional rear-end or secondary collisions as drivers behind you must brake unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to turn green.,b:Call for confirmation from another officer.,c:Follow the officer's directions and go through without stopping.,d:Refuse and follow the signal light instead.
note: A police officer directing traffic overrides traffic signals and signs. You must follow the officer’s hand signals or verbal directions, even if that means proceeding through a red light, because they are managing traffic for safety in that situation.

question: You should yield to a pedestrian:
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:Only if traffic lights favor the pedestrian.,c:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,d:At all times when necessary to prevent striking them
note: Drivers must always take care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or against a signal. You must yield whenever necessary to prevent a collision, especially in crosswalks and areas with foot traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and/or pavement markings permit passing and you have enough room to do so safely.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Pass only where signs and pavement markings indicate that passing is allowed and you have enough clear space and visibility to complete the pass without interfering with oncoming traffic or the vehicle you are passing.

question: When parking in an area not normally used for parking, you must:
options: a:Ensure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park five feet from the curb.,c:Leave your reverse lights on.
note: When you must park in an area not normally used for parking, position your vehicle so it is clearly visible to approaching drivers from all directions and does not create a hazard or obstruction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed limit and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed through without caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,c:Speed up to beat the light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if a sudden stop would cause a rear‑end collision, continue through with caution.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane and continue driving.,b:Stop in your traffic lane and flash your hazard lights.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road when possible.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, turn on your hazard lights and, when possible, steer smoothly off the roadway to a safe location away from traffic so other drivers can see you and avoid your vehicle.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign.
note: Pentagon‑shaped signs are used for school zones and school crossings, warning drivers to slow down and watch carefully for children near the roadway.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:Any amount of alcohol in your system.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Kentucky enforces zero tolerance for underage drivers; any detectable alcohol can lead to license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass another vehicle when:
options: a:There is a broken line next to your lane indicating passing is permitted.,b:There is a solid line next to your lane prohibiting passing.,c:You are on a hill or curve with limited visibility.
note: A broken (dashed) line next to your lane means you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough space to complete the pass, and obey any signs. A solid line next to your lane means no passing, and you must never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: Approaching an octagonal sign you must:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn.,c:Slow.
note: An octagon-shaped sign is used only for STOP signs. When you approach an octagonal sign, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving a parallel parking space alongside the road you should:
options: a:Not use a turn signal to avoid confusing traffic.,b:Look only in your mirrors and then go.,c:Signal your intent and look over your shoulder before moving.
note: When leaving a parallel parking space, you must signal to show other drivers you intend to pull out, then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. Only move into the lane when you are sure it is safe and there is enough space in traffic.

question: Your chest should be approximately how far from the center of the steering column?
options: a:20 inches.,b:10 to 12 inches.,c:5 inches.
note: For safety and proper airbag function, you should sit with your chest about 10–12 inches from the center of the steering wheel. This distance helps reduce the risk of injury from the airbag in a crash while still allowing you to reach the pedals and controls comfortably and maintain good control of the vehicle.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first when temperatures drop?
options: a:A tunnel.,b:An intersection.,c:A bridge.
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air can circulate both above and below the roadway, causing the pavement temperature to drop faster than on regular roads that are insulated by the ground.

question: In Kentucky, when can drivers of passenger vehicles legally use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals?
options: a:If the vehicle is not equipped with mechanical turn signals.,b:If the driver prefers to use hand signals.,c:Never (passenger vehicles must use mechanical signals).
note: Passenger vehicles are required to have working turn signal lights, but if a vehicle is not equipped with mechanical turn signals or they fail, a driver may use proper hand and arm signals to indicate turns or stops. Hand signals are a legal backup method so other road users can still understand your intentions.

question: When you spot pedestrians near the road, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the road, reduce your speed and be ready to stop. People on foot can change direction suddenly or step into the roadway, so passing slowly and cautiously gives you time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road,b:Get out of the vehicle and flag down passing cars.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get attention.,d:Exit your vehicle onto the roadway to warn others.
note: On an interstate, move completely onto the shoulder or as far off the roadway as possible, turn on your hazard flashers, and stay inside the vehicle if it is safe. High-speed traffic makes it dangerous to stand on or near the travel lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Slow and drive through if clear.,c:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,d:Ignore it and proceed as normal.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off children, drivers must:
options: a:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,b:Stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop only if children are present.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions must stop because children may be crossing the road. Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. However, on a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the barrier may proceed with caution.

question: Is it advisable to always drive more slowly than surrounding traffic?
options: a:Yes — always drive slower as a defensive technique.,b:Yes — driving more slowly is always safer than faster driving.,c:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be hazardous.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as driving too fast. It can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of a crash. Adjust your speed to the legal limit and road conditions, but do not drive unreasonably slowly and block traffic.

question: In foggy conditions, what lighting choice improves safety?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers.,b:Use low beam headlights.,c:Use parking lights only.,d:Use high beam headlights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low-beam headlights so you can see and be seen. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Parking lights or hazard flashers alone do not provide enough forward lighting or make your vehicle clearly visible to others.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:To warn another driver of danger.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision, such as when another driver may not see you. Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog, because the sudden sound can startle them and make it harder for them to judge traffic safely. Instead, slow down, yield, and give them plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Yield only to vehicles on the left.,d:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield, and cross the intersection carefully, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never; always insist on it.,b:Only when directed by an officer.,c:Only at marked intersections.,d:Often
note: You must be prepared to yield your legal right-of-way whenever it helps avoid a collision. Even if the law says you have the right-of-way, you should let the other driver go if they are not yielding or if insisting on your right-of-way could cause a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into:
options: a:Any lane you choose.,b:The second lane on the one-way street.,c:The first available lane on the one-way street.,d:The lane closest to the left curb on the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the first legal lane in your direction of travel. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles already in the other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a left-turn lane and there is oncoming traffic, you should:
options: a:Turn your front wheels left in preparation to turn.,b:Move left of the center lane to make space for the turn.,c:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your front wheels straight until turning.
note: When waiting in a left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, signal in advance and keep your front wheels straight. If you are hit from behind while your wheels are turned, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Turn the wheels only as you actually begin the turn.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:To reduce vehicle speed by roughening the road.,b:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:To alert inattentive drivers by vibration and sound when leaving the travel lane.,d:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
note: Rumble strips are grooves or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are designed to alert inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in your mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using only your mirrors, usually along the rear sides. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder to check these areas so you do not move into a space already occupied by another vehicle.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic light means you may:
options: a:Not turn in the arrow's direction until the light changes.,b:Turn after coming to a full stop.,c:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,d:Turn if the intersection is clear.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow appears. Treat it like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

question: Before changing lanes you should check mirrors and also:
options: a:Signal only after starting to move.,b:Glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.,d:Always slow down significantly.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that mirrors may not show, reducing the risk of sideswipe collisions.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More sober.,b:Less likely to be detected.,c:More intoxicated.,d:More coordinated.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in your blood. As BAC increases, your judgment, reaction time, coordination, and overall driving ability become more impaired, meaning you are more intoxicated and less safe to drive.

question: If you drive more slowly than the normal flow of traffic, what is the most likely outcome?
options: a:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,b:You will be rewarded by police.,c:You will improve traffic flow.,d:You will interfere with traffic and may receive a ticket.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of crashes. If you block or interfere with normal traffic flow without a valid reason, you may be cited. Use the right lane and match the safe, legal flow when possible.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
options: a:Only in a marked crosswalk.,b:In a marked or unmarked crosswalk and be prepared to yield to pedestrians already crossing the street.,c:Only crossing a specific lane.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and at unmarked crosswalks at intersections. Even outside crosswalks, you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians already in the roadway to avoid a collision. Always approach crosswalks and areas with pedestrians with extra caution.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while slowing or stopping to avoid them.,b:Start to prepare to slow down only.,c:Swerve around them immediately.,d:Flash your headlights.
note: If a child is about to run into the street, you must immediately slow down and be prepared to stop while also using your horn to warn them. The horn alerts the child and others, but your primary responsibility is to control your speed and avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on state highways is:
options: a:75 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:65 mph.
note: Speed limits on state highways vary by state; many states use 55 mph, 60 mph, 65 mph, or higher as the default. You must always follow the posted speed limit for the specific road you are on, because there is no single universal default limit for all U.S. state highways.

question: Changing lanes from one lane to another is best done:
options: a:When a car is in your blind spot.,b:Gradually and carefully.,c:Quickly and often.
note: Lane changes should be made gradually and carefully. Signal in advance, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and move smoothly into the next lane only when it is safe.

question: A driver's license should be considered a:
options: a:Requirement.,b:Right,c:Privilege
note: A driver’s license is a privilege, not a right. The state grants you permission to drive if you meet the requirements, and that privilege can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least:
options: a:0.10 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.05 percent.
note: For drivers age 21 or older in most U.S. states, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even at lower levels, alcohol can impair driving, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When, if ever, may you drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,d:When signs permit it.
note: You must not use the shoulder as a travel lane or to pass. The shoulder is for emergencies, breakdowns, or as directed by law enforcement. Passing on the shoulder is dangerous because other drivers do not expect moving traffic there and may pull onto it suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain speed and position regardless of danger.,c:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return safely to the drive lane.
note: If someone is passing you illegally, your job is to help avoid a crash, not to enforce the law. Gently slow down if needed and give the passing driver space to return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or block them, and do not stop in the roadway unless necessary to avoid a collision.

question: When driving in fog or mist you should avoid using high beam headlights because:
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you as well.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.
note: In fog or mist, high beams make it harder to see because the light reflects off the water droplets and back into your eyes, creating glare. Use low-beam headlights so you can see the road and be seen by others without excessive reflection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin reducing speed as you prepare to exit the interstate?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:Only after the exit ramp ends.,d:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Stay at freeway speed until you reach the deceleration lane so you do not disrupt fast-moving traffic on the main roadway. Once you are fully in the deceleration lane, begin slowing to the posted exit or advisory speed in time to safely navigate the ramp.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck, you should be prepared to:
options: a:Signal them to move faster.,b:Expect them to exceed the speed limit.,c:Pass them on the right.,d:Stop at all railroad crossings.
note: School buses and many tank trucks carrying flammable or hazardous materials are required by law to stop at all railroad crossings, even if no train is coming. When you follow these vehicles, be ready to slow down and stop behind them at tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street you should position your vehicle:
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline (in the lane closest to the center).,c:To the left of the centerline.
note: For a left turn from a two‑way street, you should be in the lane closest to the centerline. This positions you correctly for turning across oncoming traffic and helps prevent conflicts with vehicles going straight or turning right from the right lane.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Balance.,c:Judgment.,d:Hearing.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision‑making, even before you feel or notice other effects. Poor judgment leads to risky choices such as speeding, following too closely, or misjudging gaps in traffic, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: Excessive speed often:
options: a:Does not change crash risk.,b:Increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:Leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash likelihood.
note: Excessive speed reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and increases the distance needed to stop. It also makes any mistake more serious, so crashes are more likely and more severe when you drive too fast for conditions.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They are only a hazard to cyclists.,b:They only cause visibility issues.,c:They generally affect only large vehicles.,d:They can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, especially at higher speeds, and can cause drivers to drift out of their lane. While large vehicles and motorcycles are more affected, all vehicles can be destabilized by strong crosswinds or blowing debris.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds—to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. This helps you anticipate lane changes, recognize fast‑approaching vehicles, and react early to potential hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop and inch forward until you can see clearly both ways.,b:Maintain speed and rely on other drivers to stop.,c:Sound your horn and proceed quickly.,d:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.
note: When your view is blocked at an intersection, you must stop first, then move forward slowly until you can clearly see cross traffic. Creep forward a little at a time, checking both directions, and only proceed when you are sure it is safe.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the roadway but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.,b:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.,c:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
note: When a pedestrian is in the roadway and a vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction, you must not try to pass between them. Slow down, let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then move around the pedestrian only when you have enough clear space and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane without checking.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Animals near the roadway can move suddenly into your path or be followed by others you do not see yet. Slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop. Do not swerve abruptly or speed up toward the animals.

question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Turn off your headlights.,c:Set the parking brake.,d:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
note: Before stopping for a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know what traffic is doing behind and beside you. Then ease off the accelerator and apply the brakes smoothly so drivers behind you have time to react and stop safely.

question: To improve visibility in heavy rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: In heavy rain or fog, always use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle visible to others without causing glare. High beams reflect off water droplets or fog and can actually reduce how far you can see.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop whether or not children are present.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn as you pass children.
note: School crossing signs mean children may be crossing or walking near the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop if they enter the roadway. You do not always have to stop if no children are present, and you should never routinely sound your horn at children.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel so you can maintain control and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not brake hard or swerve. Ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, then steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently when the car has slowed.

question: Which action helps prevent you from becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Drive above the posted speed limit.,b:Honk repeatedly at slow drivers.,c:Relax and concentrate on driving.,d:Tailgate the driver in front of you.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay calm, give yourself extra time, and focus on safe driving rather than on other drivers’ mistakes. Speeding, tailgating, and honking in anger increase risk and are examples of aggressive driving behaviors.

question: Under foggy, low-visibility conditions you should:
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed to get out of the fog quickly.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights so the light does not reflect back and reduce your visibility. High beams make it harder to see in fog. If visibility becomes very poor, pull completely off the road to a safe place and turn on your hazard lights.

question: Which of the following is considered a driving distraction?
options: a:Only use of electronic devices.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,d:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, including visual (looking away), manual (taking hands off the wheel), or cognitive (thinking about something else). Electronic devices are one example, but eating, adjusting controls, or talking with passengers can also be distractions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection marked with a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,b:Always come to a complete stop whether traffic is present or not.,c:Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, giving the right‑of‑way to any cross traffic that is close enough to be a hazard. If traffic is clear or far enough away, you may proceed without stopping, but you must stop if needed to avoid interfering with other road users.

question: If you are driving alongside another vehicle in a multi-lane road, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay alongside them.,b:Ask the other driver to slow down.,c:Move ahead or drop back so you are not beside the other vehicle.
note: Driving side‑by‑side with another vehicle can place you in their blind spot and limits both drivers’ ability to maneuver in an emergency. It is safer to either move ahead of the other vehicle or slow slightly to fall behind, so you are not directly beside them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds regardless of distance.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:As soon as you are past the bumper.,d:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After passing on the left, you should not return to the right lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror and there is enough space between you. This helps ensure you do not cut off the other driver and that you have completed the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for a big gap before entering.,b:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge when clear.,c:Reduce speed to 25 mph before entering the lane.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance and acceleration lane to build up speed so you match the flow of traffic. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Stopping on the ramp is dangerous because freeway drivers do not expect stopped vehicles.

question: Which of the following is the correct way to use your feet when driving?
options: a:Use your left foot for braking.,b:Always brake abruptly to stop quickly.,c:Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake.
note: In normal passenger vehicles with automatic or manual transmissions, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals by mistake and gives you better control for smooth, gradual braking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:
options: a:Knowledge only.,b:License status immediately.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.,d:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reactions and interfere with clear thinking and body control. Judgment, coordination, and the ability to make safe driving decisions are affected before you feel obviously drunk, which is why any drinking can make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,b:Keeping a steady speed.,c:Using public transportation instead of driving.,d:Slowing down to look at a collision (rubbernecking).
note: Rubbernecking—slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual—forces traffic behind you to slow or brake suddenly, creating congestion and sometimes causing more collisions. Keeping a steady speed and avoiding unnecessary lane changes help traffic flow smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while a traffic signal shows green, you should:
options: a:Follow what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Obey the officer's directions.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer tells you to stop, you must stop even if the light is green. This ensures safety at the scene and is required by law.

question: When a school bus ahead stops to load or unload children with red lights flashing and the stop arm out, you must:
options: a:Change lanes,b:Come to a complete stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing at this time is illegal because children may be crossing the road and can be hard to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should be sure:
options: a:You can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:You look over your shoulder only.,c:The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
note: After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return safely without cutting it off.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Slam on the brakes before entering the water.,b:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through the water.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never drive through flooded roadways. Even a few inches of moving water can sweep a vehicle away or hide deep holes, debris, or washed‑out pavement. The safest action is to turn around and find another route.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Stop and yield, then proceed when safe; you do not wait for green.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe. You do not wait for the light to turn green, and you may not just slow down and roll through.

question: On a multilane road where there is a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does it mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only by traffic next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the dashed line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: When an approaching car has very bright headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, do not look directly at them. Briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes, helping you avoid being blinded while staying in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get ahead of them.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Pull to the right and pass them.,d:Wait until the pedestrians have finished crossing.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they clear the roadway.

question: In a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Block the lane to prevent others from passing.,c:Refuse to move your vehicle for any reason.,d:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
note: After a minor collision with no injuries and drivable vehicles, you should move your car out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so. Clearing the lane reduces the risk of another crash, keeps traffic flowing, and is allowed or required in many states for minor, non‑injury crashes.

question: Pavement is especially treacherous and slippery:
options: a:After it has been raining for several hours.,b:When it is clean and dry.,c:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Roads are most slippery just after it starts to rain, especially in the first 10–30 minutes. Oil and residue on the pavement mix with the water and create a slick surface. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, you should:
options: a:Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.,b:Check mirrors only.,c:Signal only and then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal to alert other road users, then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is clear and safe. Relying on mirrors alone or signaling without checking blind spots can lead to collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park uphill where there is a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping stop the car and keeping it from rolling into traffic.

question: If the road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:
options: a:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,b:Two feet shorter than usual.,c:Closer than normal.,d:The same as normal.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and your stopping distance increases. To give yourself enough time and space to brake smoothly without skidding, you should increase your following distance and stay farther behind the vehicle ahead than you normally would on dry pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow center lines to pass another vehicle when:
options: a:The yellow line next to the opposite lane is broken.,b:The yellow line next to your lane is broken.,c:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
note: Double yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may only pass when the yellow line next to your lane is broken, and only if it is safe and legal to do so. If the solid line is on your side, you must not cross it to pass, even if the other side has a broken line.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn fully and look out the back window.,c:Ignore rear traffic unless merging.,d:Only check blind spots.
note: To drive defensively, you need to know what is happening behind you as well as in front. Frequently checking your rearview mirror lets you see vehicles that are gaining on you, preparing to pass, or following too closely, so you can adjust your speed or lane position safely.

question: Before driving, remove all snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:All windows and mirrors.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Only the hood and roof.,d:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Snow, frost, and ice on any window or mirror can block your view and create dangerous blind spots. Before driving, clear all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in every direction and can see other road users, traffic signals, and hazards clearly.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you turn on to be seen?
options: a:Up the instrument panel lights.,b:On your parking lights.,c:On your headlights.,d:On your hazard lights.
note: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, visibility is reduced and it is harder for others to see you. Turn on your headlights—using low beams—so you can see the road and so your vehicle is more visible to oncoming traffic and vehicles ahead of you. Many states also require headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers who are turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight or with the right-of-way.,b:Overtaking cars only.,c:No one; the turning driver always has the right-of-way.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way unless you have a protected green arrow or are otherwise clearly given priority.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only if a crossing guard is present.,b:Only at marked crosswalks.,c:At all times.,d:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and must be given the right-of-way at all times. You must stop and allow them to cross safely, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk or a crossing guard.

question: Allow extra following space when you are behind a:
options: a:Convertible.,b:Motorcycle.,c:Station wagon.,d:Passenger vehicle.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see, and they can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. Leave extra following distance so you have more time to react if the rider brakes suddenly or loses control.

question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:The same as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, possessing or consuming open containers of alcohol is:
options: a:Allowed for passengers only.,b:Legal if the driver is not intoxicated.,c:Illegal.,d:Legal if you are not driving.
note: Open container laws generally make it illegal for anyone in a moving vehicle on a public road to possess or drink from an open container of alcohol. Even if the driver is sober, open containers in the passenger area can be a violation.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, you should:
options: a:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to restore traction.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking until traction returns.,c:Shift into a lower gear immediately to slow down.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), gently ease off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or make sudden turns, because that can cause a skid. Wait until you feel the tires regain traction before braking or changing direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, how do you check your blind spot?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely solely on the side mirror.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show the entire area around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot where vehicles or motorcycles may be hidden from your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,b:Sound your horn and pass quickly.,c:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,d:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.
note: If a vehicle has stopped at a crosswalk, assume there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see. You must not pass the stopped vehicle. Stop as well and proceed only after you are sure all pedestrians have completely crossed and the crosswalk is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:You have passed the vehicle's front bumper.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Speed up and expect other drivers to make room.,b:Check behind you and then watch the vehicle ahead before moving.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: When entering a gap in highway traffic, you must check traffic behind and to the sides, then watch the vehicle ahead in the lane you are entering. Adjust your speed so you can smoothly merge into the gap without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: What do broken yellow center lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and allow passing when safe.,b:They indicate no passing zones.,c:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle if it is legal and you can do so safely with enough clear distance ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Stop on the ramp and wait for a gap to return.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route; do not back up.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm and keep going to the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop, back up on the freeway, or reverse on the shoulder. Exit safely at the next opportunity and then find a route back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass stopped vehicles without stopping.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Stop
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must actively scan to the left and right to see pedestrians, cyclists, trains, and other vehicles that may cross your path. Looking to the sides helps you spot hazards early so you can slow or stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if you and a driver on your left arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You have the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other driver is on your left, that means you are on their right, so you may proceed first after making a complete stop and ensuring it is safe.

question: What is the only medically proven method to lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Get fresh air or take a cold shower.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Allow your body time to process the alcohol.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; coffee, cold showers, food, or fresh air do not speed this process or make you sober enough to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection you should:
options: a:Only yield to vehicles,b:Assume oncoming traffic must yield to you.,c:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,d:Never yield; complete the turn quickly.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only turn when there is a safe gap and the path is clear.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled roadway if possible.,c:Turn off your emergency flashers immediately.,d:Leave the vehicle where it stopped.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, you should move it as far off the traveled portion of the road as possible, ideally with all four wheels off the roadway, and turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle when:
options: a:You have just barely passed the vehicle's front bumper.,b:You can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return safely without cutting the other driver off.

question: Collisions become more likely when:
options: a:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,b:One lane travels slightly faster than the other lanes consistently.,c:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
note: Crash risk increases when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic, because it creates more passing, lane changes, and sudden braking. When all vehicles travel at about the same speed within the speed limit, traffic flow is smoother and safer.

question: If you are prescribed a medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Avoid taking any medications.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,d:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about its effects on driving.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist whether a medication can affect your driving before you drive after taking it.

question: When exiting the freeway on a downhill curved ramp you should:
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Stop at the start of the ramp.,c:Slow only after you enter the curve.,d:Reduce speed to the freeway posted limit.
note: When exiting a freeway on a downhill, curved ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve, especially going downhill, can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid. Enter the ramp at a controlled speed so you can steer smoothly through the curve.

question: When should you reduce speed when approaching a curve?
options: a:Before entering the curve.,b:Only if you feel like it.,c:When you are halfway through the curve.,d:After you are in the curve.
note: You should always reduce speed before entering a curve. If you wait to slow down until you are already turning, you may have to brake while the vehicle is leaning, which can reduce traction and increase the risk of skidding. Enter the curve at a safe speed, then maintain a steady speed or gently accelerate through it.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed so:
options: a:Other drivers can merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck has room to stop safely.,c:Other drivers can slow down without consequence.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than smaller vehicles because of their size and weight. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver enough room to slow or stop safely if traffic changes. Cutting closely in front of a truck or following too closely reduces this safety margin and increases the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: In rainy weather, when are you most likely to skid while turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: The road surface is often most slippery during the first half hour of rain. Oil, grease, and other residues on the road mix with the fresh water and create a slick layer, which makes skidding more likely when turning or stopping. As rain continues, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should always drive cautiously on wet roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning left at a red light after a complete stop is allowed only when:
options: a:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.,b:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it.
note: In many U.S. states, you may turn left on a red light only when you are on a one-way street turning left onto another one-way street, after coming to a complete stop and only if there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You must yield to all oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.

question: Adjust the driver's seat so you can see the pavement how far in front of your vehicle?
options: a:12 to 15 inches.,b:5 to 10 feet.,c:12 to 15 feet.
note: Adjust your seat so you can see the road surface a short distance in front of your vehicle, typically about 12 to 15 feet. This helps you judge where the front of your vehicle is, while still keeping your eyes primarily on the road ahead. You should also sit so your chest is about 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel to allow the air bag to deploy safely and to maintain good control.

question: You are following a motorcycle and want to pass. What should you do?
options: a:Remain in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.,b:Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.,c:Sound your horn to force the motorcycle onto the shoulder.
note: Treat a motorcycle as you would any other vehicle: it is entitled to a full lane. When passing, move completely into the left lane, just as you would when passing a car, and do not share the lane or crowd the motorcycle. Return to your lane only when you can see the motorcycle clearly in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Always yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk with the right-of-way. Do not start your turn until it is safe and the path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right, the best action is to:
options: a:Maintain your speed and position in the right lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when it is safe.,c:Slow down in the right lane.
note: When traffic permits, move to the left lane to allow merging vehicles room to enter from on-ramps on your right.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Only if you are stopped and cited.,b:Only if you are involved in a collision.,c:Whenever asked after a traffic stop or after a collision.
note: You must carry proof of insurance (financial responsibility) in your vehicle and show it to a law enforcement officer whenever requested, whether during a traffic stop or after a collision. Failing to provide proof when asked can result in citations or other penalties.

question: When poor weather reduces visibility, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, fog, snow, or darkness, you need more space to see and react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra time to notice hazards and brake smoothly, which helps prevent rear‑end collisions. Speeding up or driving closer to oncoming traffic is dangerous because you have less time and space to respond if something unexpected happens.

question: Only which of the following can reduce blood alcohol concentration and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Eating fatty foods.,b:Time.,c:Drinking coffee.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Your liver can handle only a certain amount per hour, and nothing you eat or drink can speed that up. Coffee, cold showers, or food might make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you a safe driver.

question: How often is it recommended you glance at your speedometer while driving?
options: a:Continuously.,b:Frequently with quick glances while keeping your main focus on the road.,c:Once a minute.,d:Once every ten minutes.
note: Safe drivers check their speed regularly but briefly so they can stay within the speed limit without taking their eyes off the road for long. You should glance at your speedometer often enough to control your speed, especially when conditions or limits change, but never stare at it continuously or wait many minutes between checks. Keep each glance quick and return your focus to the traffic around you.

question: When a large truck ahead begins a right turn onto a street with two lanes in each direction, the truck:
options: a:May need to swing wide to the left before completing the right turn.,b:May complete the turn in either lane without adjusting.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Large trucks need more space to turn because their rear wheels track inside the path of the front wheels. To avoid hitting the curb or parked cars, a truck may swing wide to the left before making a right turn. You should never try to squeeze between the truck and the curb or between the truck and its left side while it is turning; give it plenty of room to complete the maneuver.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent will:
options: a:Increase your chances of being in an accident compared with having no alcohol in your system.,b:Have no effect on your driving.,c:Never put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. A BAC around 0.02 percent has been shown to measurably increase crash risk compared with sober driving, so it is not safe to assume such a level has no effect. Because any alcohol can impair driving ability, the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Wait — allow time for your body to metabolize it.
note: Time is the only method that lowers blood alcohol concentration; other measures do not speed elimination.

question: Which factor listed affects how a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:The person's weight.,b:The person's intelligence.,c:The person's height.
note: A person's weight, sex, food in the stomach, and number of drinks consumed affect alcohol absorption and BAC.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should keep your headlights set to:
options: a:High beam until within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,b:High beam at all times.,c:Low beam.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver ahead; use high beams only when no vehicles are nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires that drivers:
options: a:Drive the same as on surface streets.,b:Only be able to drive at increased speeds.,c:Be constantly alert and be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
note: Safe interstate driving requires both constant alertness and the ability to operate safely at the higher speeds of highway traffic.

question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.,b:Slow down significantly before moving.,c:Check only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Always check mirrors and blind spots by glancing over your shoulder to ensure a lane change is safe.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:The crossing is in a city or town.,b:There isn't room on the other side for you to clear the tracks.,c:You are transporting two or more young children only.,d:The train signals are silent.
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. If there is not enough room on the far side of the tracks for your entire vehicle to clear them, you must stop and wait before the tracks. Only proceed when you are sure you can drive completely across without stopping.

question: What may happen if you take prescription medication while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It will make you more alert.,b:It will have no effect.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can interact with alcohol and greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, or slow reaction time. Combining them can make you unsafe to drive even if each one alone might be legal to use.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Because large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop and may not stop in time.,c:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than cars and need a longer distance to stop. If you brake suddenly in front of them, the driver may not be able to stop in time, increasing the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
