question: Which of the following should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal before changing lanes.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,d:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and other drivers may not expect it. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating other vehicles and failing to watch for workers and equipment.,b:Using turn signals.,c:Driving below the posted speed.
note: In work zones, traffic patterns can change and workers or equipment may be close to the roadway. Tailgating reduces your time to react if traffic slows or stops suddenly, making crashes more likely. Always leave extra space and stay alert for workers and machinery.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What is the first action you should take?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal to increase space.,b:Swerve into the adjacent lane immediately.,c:Sound your horn and brake hard.
note: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator. This increases the space between you and the other vehicle without sudden braking or swerving, which could cause a rear-end collision or loss of control. After creating space, you can brake smoothly if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a left turn at an upcoming corner, you must yield to:
options: a:Only vehicles approaching from the right.,b:Only oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:Pedestrians and any vehicles that have the right-of-way.
note: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk, bicyclists, and all oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard, including those going straight or turning right. Only complete your turn when the way is clear and you will not interfere with others who have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Avoid driving alongside it for long stretches.,b:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,c:Pass only on the right.,d:Follow it closely to reduce wind drag.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along their sides, especially on the right. Avoid driving next to them for long periods so the driver can see you and you have room to react if they need to change lanes or stop. Pass safely and promptly, and never follow large vehicles too closely.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect the unexpected and proceed with caution.
note: In construction zones, slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, lane shifts, workers, and equipment, and follow all posted signs and flagger directions. Expect unusual or changing conditions and drive with extra caution to protect both workers and other road users.

question: If you suffer a sudden tire blowout, you should:
options: a:Use the brakes lightly and gradually slow down.,b:Pump the brakes quickly.,c:Apply the brakes fully and immediately.
note: During a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease off the accelerator. Once the vehicle slows and you have control, brake gently and steer to a safe place off the road. Sudden or hard braking can cause loss of control, especially at higher speeds.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Coordination only.,b:Both alertness and coordination.,c:None of the above.,d:Alertness only.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time and reduce both alertness and coordination. Because safe driving depends on being able to notice hazards quickly and control the vehicle smoothly, any impairment to alertness or coordination makes driving dangerous.

question: To help prevent skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Speed up going into curves and slow to exit them.,b:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,c:Shift into a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,d:Avoid slowing down on slippery roads.
note: On slippery roads, sudden braking or steering while you are already in a curve can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid. You should slow down before you enter curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly and brake gently if needed.

question: At night you should:
options: a:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Drive at the same speed and following distance you use in daylight.
note: At night, visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge speed and distance, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use low beams when following or meeting other vehicles to avoid glare, and use high beams only when they will not blind other drivers.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, they may:
options: a:Only wait on the side of the road.,b:Cut through all lanes of traffic without yielding.,c:Use the left lane or left portion of the lane as needed to make the turn when safe.,d:Make left turns only by walking the bicycle in a crosswalk.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. When making a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the appropriate left-turn lane or left portion of the lane, signal, and turn like any other vehicle when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,b:Mirrors fully remove blind spots.,c:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.,d:Blind spots can be checked using only the rearview mirror.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that cannot be seen in mirrors alone, and large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars. You should avoid lingering in these areas and always turn your head to check blind spots before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. If you move into the intersection and then have to stop, you can block cross traffic and create a hazard, which is illegal in many jurisdictions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not enter an intersection if doing so will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:You may enter only if you can clear the intersection without blocking cross traffic.,b:You may enter if you think the light will stay green.,c:You should not enter if doing so will cause you to block the intersection when the light turns red.
note: You may enter an intersection on a green light even if it later turns yellow or red, as long as you had a green when you entered and you are not entering so far that you will block cross traffic. The key rule is: do not enter the intersection unless you are reasonably sure you can clear it without stopping and blocking other vehicles when the light changes.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving distracting?
options: a:It causes the driver to be concerned about the call cost.,b:It reduces engine performance.,c:It draws the attention of other drivers.,d:It takes your attention away from driving and can take your hands and eyes off the road.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is distracting because it takes your hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your mind off driving. Even hands‑free calls can reduce your attention to traffic conditions, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: Tailgating (following too closely) often:
options: a:Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,b:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:Is the best way to signal impatience.,d:Can frustrate other drivers and lead to aggressive behavior.
note: Following too closely increases the chance of a rear‑end collision and often angers or frustrates other drivers. This can escalate into aggressive driving or road rage, making the situation more dangerous for everyone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multi-lane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should begin the turn from:
options: a:Any lane as long as it's safe.,b:The center lane of the road.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, you should start from the lane closest to the left curb and turn into the nearest lane on the new street that is also closest to the left curb. This keeps traffic organized and reduces conflicts with other vehicles.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines mean:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the right only.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the left only.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that vehicles in both directions must stay in their lane and may not cross the lines to pass. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road where it is otherwise legal and safe.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy weather, you should:
options: a:Move onto the shoulder as soon as it begins to rain.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to reduce this risk is to slow down, especially in heavy rain or standing water, and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: In bad weather, you should:
options: a:Steer off the road immediately.,b:Drive in a lower gear at all times.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.,d:Brake hard to reduce speed quickly.
note: In bad weather, sudden steering, acceleration, or hard braking can cause you to lose traction and skid. Steer and brake smoothly and gently so your tires maintain grip on the road and you keep better control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (right).,b:Keep them pointed straight ahead.,c:Away from the edge of the road.
note: When parking facing uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will move toward the shoulder instead of back into traffic.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely only on the outside mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder.,c:Use parking sensors only.,d:Trust the inside rearview mirror.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure there is no vehicle in your blind spot, then change lanes if it is clear.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Speed up to clear the crosswalk.,c:Expect them to yield to you.,d:Honk to let them know you are there.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed, never honk, rush through, or expect them to move for you. Give them extra time and space to cross safely.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) safety belt system, you should:
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Wear both the lap and shoulder belts.
note: Lap and shoulder belts are designed to work together. The lap belt keeps your lower body in place, and the shoulder belt keeps your upper body from striking the steering wheel, dashboard, or windshield. Using both greatly reduces the risk of serious injury.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction due to water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.,b:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to stop the sliding.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually; do not brake or turn suddenly. Wait until you feel the tires regain traction before braking or making normal steering corrections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed through the intersection without stopping.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must come to a safe stop. Only proceed if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

question: Which best defines distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,d:Anything that improves driving performance.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, including taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off the driving task. Even brief distractions can greatly increase your risk of a crash.

question: Roads and highways are most slippery when:
options: a:It has been raining heavily for several hours.,b:They are clean and dry.,c:It has just begun to rain.
note: Roads are usually most slippery just after it starts to rain because oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the first water and rise to the top, reducing traction. After it has been raining for a while, much of this residue is washed away and the road surface generally becomes less slippery, though still wet.

question: There is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead. You should:
options: a:Slow down and pass carefully.,b:Make eye contact then pass in front of them.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Speed up to pass before they cross.
note: Even without marked crosswalks, you must yield and allow pedestrians to finish crossing safely.

question: Your car may begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at relatively low speeds, often around 35 mph, especially when there is standing water and tires are worn or underinflated. Once hydroplaning starts, your tires lose contact with the road and you can lose steering and braking control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers entering interstate traffic from an acceleration ramp do?
options: a:Have the right-of-way.,b:Come to a full stop at the end of the ramp before entering.,c:Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,d:May force their way into traffic.
note: When entering an interstate from an acceleration lane, you must adjust your speed to match traffic and yield to vehicles already on the highway. Merge only when there is a safe gap; traffic on the interstate has the right-of-way.

question: A good driver should:
options: a:Only focus straight ahead.,b:Watch all around, including beside and behind your vehicle.,c:Stare directly ahead all the time.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan all around their vehicle—ahead, to the sides, and behind—so they can spot hazards early and react in time. Focusing only straight ahead or only on one area of the road reduces your ability to see changing conditions and other road users.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Keep cruise control on.
note: On wet or icy roads, your tires have much less grip, so it takes longer to stop and your vehicle can skid more easily. Reducing your speed and driving smoothly gives you more time to react and helps prevent loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but can't find a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to make room.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,d:Back up on the ramp to get a better view.
note: You must not stop in a freeway lane, but it is legal and safer to stop at the end of the entrance ramp if you cannot find a safe gap. Do not force your way into traffic or back up on the ramp. Wait at the end of the ramp until there is a large enough opening, then accelerate quickly to match freeway speed as you merge.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up because the lane ends ahead.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment and reduce your speed.
note: Orange signs and cones mean you are entering a work zone. Lanes may shift, narrow, or end, and workers or equipment may be close to traffic. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow all posted work-zone signs and directions.

question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,b:Drive on the interstate to release stress.,c:Loudly play the radio while driving to distract yourself.,d:Drive faster to get over the anger quickly.
note: Strong emotions like anger reduce your concentration and increase risky behavior behind the wheel. It is safest to wait until you have calmed down before driving so you can focus fully on the road and make good decisions.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment.,b:If you can walk straight, you are safe to drive.,c:Alcohol only affects inexperienced drivers.,d:Being under the legal BAC means your driving is not impaired.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, coordination, and reaction time, even at low blood alcohol levels. You can be unsafe to drive even if you are under the legal BAC limit or feel fine. The only safe assumption is that any drinking can impair your ability to drive.

question: When a centerline is marked with a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line, passing is:
options: a:Prohibited from both directions.,b:Allowed only from the side beside the broken yellow line.,c:Allowed from either side at any time.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe. Traffic on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, you should steer:
options: a:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on the left and parked cars on the right, you should position your vehicle near the center of your lane. This gives you the greatest possible space cushion from both the oncoming vehicles and the parked cars.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally (not in a crosswalk), you must:
options: a:Proceed because they are violating the law.,b:Stop and yield to them.,c:Flash your lights and continue.,d:Honk to force them to move.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing illegally, you must slow or stop to avoid hitting them. Drivers are always responsible for preventing a collision with pedestrians when possible, regardless of who has the right-of-way.

question: A school bus stopped in your lane with red lights flashing means you should:
options: a:Stop and proceed when the red lights stop flashing and the bus signals it is safe.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing and until the bus resumes motion, the driver signals you to proceed, or the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm (if present) is withdrawn. Do not move again just because you think children are done exiting; wait until the bus signals that it is safe by turning off the red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking an intersection while you face a green light, what should you do?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection until you can completely clear it.,b:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,c:Partially enter to establish right-of-way.,d:Honk and push through.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. You should wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to clear the intersection completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice when driving on an interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,b:Proceeding to the next exit if you miss yours.,c:Changing lanes without signaling.
note: Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and usually illegal because other drivers cannot anticipate your movement. On interstates, slower traffic should stay in the right lane, and if you miss your exit you must continue to the next one rather than stopping or backing up.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, you should turn your wheels:
options: a:Keep them straight.,b:Away from the curb.,c:Toward the curb or side of the road.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll into the curb or away from traffic instead of into the lane.

question: When traveling through a work zone you should:
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,c:Pass as soon as you get a chance.
note: In work zones, slow down and leave extra following distance so you have time to react to sudden stops, lane shifts, or workers and equipment near the roadway. Tailgating or trying to pass aggressively is dangerous in these areas.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:None; alcohol has no effect.,b:Three.,c:One.,d:Two.
note: Even one alcoholic drink can slow your reaction time, reduce judgment, and affect coordination. Any amount of alcohol can impair driving ability, so you should not drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed. You must yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right of way before moving through the intersection.

question: When parking next to a curb, when must you use your turn signals?
options: a:When pulling next to,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling away from the curb.
note: Drivers should signal any time they move toward or away from the curb so other road users can anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a vehicle entering your interstate lane from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Ignore them since you have the right-of-way.,b:Speed up to pass them before they merge.,c:Change lanes if possible to allow them room to merge.
note: When another vehicle is entering from an on‑ramp, you should help the flow of traffic by changing lanes if it is safe, giving them space to merge smoothly.

question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Squeeze between it and the curb.,b:Quickly turn ahead of the truck or bus.,c:Wait until the truck or bus completes the turn before you turn.,d:Honk to make it stop turning.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to turn; do not try to cut between them and the curb or you risk a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you make a left turn when on a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as you signal.,c:The lane nearest the center of the street.,d:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: On a one‑way street, left turns must be made from the lane closest to the left curb into the nearest appropriate lane on the road you are entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When overtaking another vehicle going the same direction, you should:
options: a:Pass as slowly as possible to avoid surprises.,b:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible before returning to the lane.,c:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
note: When passing, move into the passing lane, accelerate to complete the pass safely and promptly, then return only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What message is shown on a red, octagon-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:Stop.,c:One-way.
note: A red octagon is the universal STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Prevents skidding entirely.,c:Locks the front wheels and causes a loss of steering.,d:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice and snow, hard continuous braking can cause the wheels to lock. When the front wheels lock, you lose steering control and the vehicle will tend to slide straight ahead. To maintain control, brake gently and early, and if you have ABS, press the brake firmly and let the system work.

question: Reaction time is slower after:
options: a:Working hard.,b:Drinking alcohol.,c:Exercising.,d:Sleeping.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain and nervous system. After drinking, your reaction time increases, your reflexes are slower, and your judgment and vision are reduced, which makes it much harder to respond quickly to hazards while driving.

question: If a child is bicycling near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.,b:Beep your horn to warn them.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden movements.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your lane without warning. Slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared for sudden movements instead of assuming they are fully in control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is allowed from both directions.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing from either side. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when instructed by traffic control, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: Under normal conditions, maintain a following distance of at least:
options: a:Three seconds.,b:Five seconds.,c:Two seconds.,d:One second.
note: Under normal, dry conditions you should stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. Pick a fixed object ahead; when the vehicle ahead passes it, you should be able to count “one‑thousand‑one, one‑thousand‑two, one‑thousand‑three” before you reach the same point. This time‑gap gives you space to see hazards and brake smoothly if traffic slows or stops.

question: Which area is most likely to become icy after snow or rain in cold weather?
options: a:A residential road.,b:A hilly road.,c:A road in a shaded area.
note: Roads in shaded areas freeze sooner and stay icy longer because sunlight cannot reach the pavement to warm and melt the ice. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, shaded spots—such as those under trees, bridges, or in deep cuts—may still be slick. Always slow down and be extra cautious when driving through shaded sections in cold, wet weather.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can do what to your driving?
options: a:Impair your judgment.,b:Improve concentration.,c:Make you feel better.,d:Help you be a better driver.
note: Drowsiness affects driving much like alcohol or drugs: it slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and impairs your judgment. A tired driver may not notice hazards in time or may make poor decisions, such as misjudging speed and distance or drifting out of their lane. The only safe choice when you are very sleepy is to stop driving and rest.

question: What should you do when driving through a highway construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Pass the construction zone carefully and avoid 'rubbernecking'.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Drive faster than the posted limit to clear the zone quickly.
note: In highway construction zones you must slow as needed, obey all signs and flaggers, and pass through carefully without “rubbernecking.” Looking away from the road to watch workers or incidents increases the risk of crashes and can cause sudden slowdowns. Maintain a safe speed and following distance, stay alert for lane shifts or workers, and focus on the roadway ahead.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Be ready to use your horn frequently.,b:Drive more slowly directly behind the motorcycle.,c:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and more vulnerable, and they can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. When following a motorcycle, leave at least a three‑ to four‑second following distance so you have enough time to react if the rider slows or stops suddenly. Extra space also helps you see the motorcycle clearly and avoid crowding it from behind.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed only for turning vehicles.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Allowed from both directions.,d:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean you must not cross the lines to pass from either direction. You may usually cross them only to turn left into or from a driveway or side road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield to cross traffic and pedestrians that are close enough to be a hazard.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let cross traffic and any pedestrians or vehicles already in or close to the intersection go first if they are close enough to be a hazard. Proceed only when you can merge or cross safely.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow quick stopping.,c:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need much more distance to stop than passenger cars, especially at higher speeds or when loaded. Drivers should avoid cutting in front of trucks or braking suddenly because the truck may not be able to stop in time.

question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Brake hard while turning.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Activate your turn signal.
note: Before entering a curve, slow to a safe speed while you are still driving straight. Entering too fast or braking hard in the curve can cause you to lose traction and control. Adjust speed first, then steer smoothly through the curve.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, you should:
options: a:Steer to the right immediately.,b:Steer to the left to regain control.,c:Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, gently steer to the left in the same direction as the skid. This helps the front wheels point where you want to go and allows the vehicle to straighten out. Avoid hard braking or jerky steering, which can make the skid worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check blind spots before changing lanes, a driver should:
options: a:Rely only on the outside mirrors.,b:Turn their head and look over the appropriate shoulder.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors first, then quickly turn your head and look over the shoulder on the side you’re moving toward to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Before you back up, you should:
options: a:Roll down all windows but not look back.,b:Check behind the vehicle before getting in.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.,d:Rely only on your mirrors.
note: Before backing, walk around or look behind your vehicle to make sure the path is clear, especially for children, pets, or low objects you cannot see from the driver’s seat. Then back up slowly while checking mirrors and looking over your shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to block an intersection?
options: a:During rush hour traffic.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You should not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Blocking an intersection can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from moving and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Stop only if children are visible.,c:Slow to 10 mph and proceed with caution.,d:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on interstate highways in Kentucky?
options: a:75 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:65 mph.,d:45 mph.
note: In Kentucky, the general speed limit on interstate highways is 65 mph unless posted otherwise. Always follow the posted speed limit, which may be higher or lower in certain areas such as urban zones or construction zones.

question: You can help the driver behind you keep a safe distance by:
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early gives drivers behind you time to react smoothly, so they can adjust their speed and following distance without sudden braking. Sudden speed changes or large speed differences make it harder for them to keep a safe space cushion.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,b:Always signal before changing lanes or turning.,c:Use your horn frequently to assert your right-of-way.
note: Using your turn signals consistently and driving courteously helps other drivers understand your intentions, which reduces confusion, frustration, and the chance of aggressive behavior. Avoid distractions and aggressive actions like frequent horn use, which can escalate road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an all-way stop, you should yield the right-of-way to any driver who:
options: a:Is on your left.,b:Is signaling to make a turn.,c:Arrived before you.
note: At an all-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. You must yield to any driver who reached the intersection before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: On a freeway you should look farther ahead than on a city street in order to:
options: a:Ignore merging traffic.,b:Reduce the need to check mirrors.,c:See potential hazards earlier.,d:Keep up with cars behind you.
note: On freeways, higher speeds mean you need more time and distance to react. By looking farther ahead, you can spot slow traffic, lane closures, or other hazards early and adjust smoothly instead of making sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What important step should you take when preparing to turn?
options: a:Always move to the left lane first.,b:Check traffic in all directions.,c:Signal only after starting the turn.,d:Increase your speed before turning.
note: Before turning, you should check traffic in all directions—ahead, to both sides, and behind—to be sure the turn is safe. Combine this with proper signaling and speed adjustment so other road users know what you plan to do and have time to react.

question: Alcohol in any concentration acts as:
options: a:A depressant.,b:Neither a depressant nor stimulant.,c:A stimulant.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is classified as a central nervous system depressant. Even in small amounts, it slows brain activity, reaction time, and coordination, and reduces judgment and alertness. It does not act as a stimulant or hallucinogen, even if some people initially feel more talkative or energetic.

question: Blue traffic signs primarily provide information about:
options: a:Mileage and distance to destinations.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services such as rest areas.,d:Recreation and cultural interest areas.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, hospitals, and other facilities that drivers may need while traveling.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:
options: a:Not turn the steering wheel at all.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. If the rear skids left, turn the steering wheel left. This helps the front wheels realign with the direction of travel and regain traction. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can make the skid worse.

question: To reduce glare from the headlights of an oncoming vehicle, you should:
options: a:Flash your high beams at the other vehicle.,b:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,c:Stare at the centerline for the whole time.
note: When facing glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using it as a guide. This helps you avoid being blinded while still keeping track of your lane position. Do not stare directly at the headlights or at the centerline.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic control signal is not working, you must:
options: a:Follow traffic flow without stopping.,b:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.,c:Proceed if the intersection appears clear.,d:Come to a full stop and treat the intersection as an all-way stop.
note: If a traffic signal is completely dark or not working, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop unless a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic. Come to a full stop, then proceed only when it is safe, yielding the right-of-way as you would at a four-way stop.

question: Driving while under the influence of medication that impairs you is:
options: a:Allowed if the medication is prescribed.,b:Allowed if you do not feel drowsy.,c:Illegal under all circumstances.
note: Driving under the influence of anything that impairs you—alcohol, illegal drugs, or prescription/over‑the‑counter medication—is illegal. The key issue is impairment, not whether a doctor prescribed the drug. If the medication affects your judgment, reaction time, or alertness, you must not drive.

question: As you approach an intersection showing a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic as necessary. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety, and you do not wait for a green light.

question: If you become tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Open your windows to stay awake.,b:Turn up the music loudly.,c:Drink coffee and continue.,d:Stop to rest or switch drivers.
note: When you feel tired while driving, the only safe choice is to stop driving—either take a rest break or switch drivers. Tricks like opening windows, loud music, or caffeine do not reliably prevent drowsy driving and can give a false sense of alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless a sign shows otherwise, the speed limit in a business or residential district in Kentucky is:
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: In Kentucky, the default speed limit in a business or residential district is 35 mph unless otherwise posted.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean for drivers on your side of the road?
options: a:You may pass on the right only.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:You must turn left only when clear.,d:Passing is never permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross the line to pass another vehicle when it is safe and the way ahead is clear of oncoming traffic. You must still judge carefully for enough space and visibility and never pass where it is unsafe, such as near hills, curves, or intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:
options: a:Using only side mirrors.,b:Using only the rearview mirror.,c:Using side mirrors and looking over your shoulder.,d:Stopping on the ramp to check traffic.
note: Use both your side mirrors and a quick glance over your shoulder to check your blind spots before merging onto a freeway. Mirrors alone cannot show every vehicle around you, so a shoulder check helps you see cars that may be hidden and lets you merge safely into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should enter at:
options: a:The legal posted limit no matter traffic.,b:Below 20 mph for safety.,c:Much more slowly than freeway traffic.,d:At or near the speed of the existing freeway traffic.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near that of traffic already on the freeway, as long as it does not exceed the posted limit. Matching the flow of traffic makes it easier and safer to find a gap and merge smoothly.

question: Drivers must obey instructions from which of these personnel at work zones?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down.,c:Flaggers (signal persons).,d:Pedestrians.
note: In work zones, you must obey the instructions of flaggers (signal persons). They are authorized to direct traffic, sometimes even over traffic signals or signs, to protect workers and drivers. Always follow their hand signals or signs and proceed with extra caution.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Because motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.,b:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:Because motorcycles do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than most cars and trucks. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles.

question: If everyone has exited your vehicle, is it acceptable to leave the engine running?
options: a:If parked in a secure lot.,b:If you will be away for less than an hour.,c:Never leave the engine running.,d:If you will only be away for a couple of minutes.
note: Kentucky law requires you to turn off the engine and remove the key when leaving a vehicle; always lock it even for short absences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Press hard on your brakes to force them to slow down.,b:Increase your speed to prevent them from passing.,c:Ease off the accelerator to help them pass safely.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, you should cooperate by maintaining a steady speed or easing off the accelerator slightly so they can pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as that can cause conflicts or collisions.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what is the safest response?
options: a:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,b:Tap or pump the brakes.,c:Steer hard immediately to the shoulder.,d:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, remove your foot from the accelerator and let the vehicle slow; apply brakes lightly only after the car has slowed.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:It is hard to judge distance and vehicle speed in the dark.
note: At night, your visibility is limited to the area lit by your headlights, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce what you see. This makes it harder to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving, increasing the risk of mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often:
options: a:Saves significant travel time.,b:Increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.,c:Helps maneuver safely around obstacles.,d:Reduces fuel consumption.
note: Driving too fast gives you less time to react and greatly increases the force of any collision, which raises the chances of serious injury or death. The time saved by speeding is usually very small compared to the increased risk.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,b:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass if it is safe and legal; a solid yellow line next to your lane means you must not pass. When one side is broken and the other is solid, only traffic on the broken-line side may pass.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, you should slow down and turn on:
options: a:Your headlights.,b:Your emergency flashers only.,c:Your parking lights.
note: In dust, smoke, or other low-visibility conditions, you should slow down and turn on your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you. Do not rely on parking lights alone, and use emergency flashers only if you are stopped or moving very slowly and creating a hazard.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:A construction zone is ahead.,d:Only buses may cross for boarding.
note: A broken yellow line in the center of a two-way road means traffic in both directions may pass when it is safe. You must check for oncoming traffic and enough clear distance before crossing the line to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When the warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Never.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. You must wait until the lights stop flashing, the gate is fully raised, and you can see that the tracks are clear before crossing.

question: If you strike a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return and then exchange information.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a note with your name, address, and contact information securely on the vehicle, then report the collision as required by law.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should occupants still do?
options: a:Not wear seat belts.,b:Wear belts behind their backs.,c:Disable the airbags.,d:Wear seat belts.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. All occupants should always wear properly adjusted lap and shoulder belts, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cough syrups only.,b:None of the above.,c:Tranquilizers and other legal or illegal drugs that can cause drowsiness or slow reactions.
note: Many different substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, some prescription drugs, and even certain over‑the‑counter cough and cold medicines. Any drug that makes you drowsy, slows your reactions, or affects your judgment can make driving unsafe, even if it is legal or prescribed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' signal flashed and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before you go.,b:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,d:Flash your horn and proceed.
note: You must yield to pedestrians and give them time to finish crossing the intersection before you proceed, even on a green light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi‑lane roads, the right lane is generally for through driving, and the left lane is mainly for passing. If you are in the center lane and traffic is passing you on both sides, you are likely going slower than the normal flow. When it is safe, move to the lane on your right so faster traffic can use the center and left lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is prohibited:
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view.
note: U‑turns are unsafe where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on or near curves or hills. Limited visibility means other drivers may not see you in time to react. Only make U‑turns where they are legal and where you have a clear view of traffic in all directions.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is retracted and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped, in most situations from both directions, until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. Children may cross unexpectedly, so you cannot proceed until the bus signals that it is safe.

question: When driving through a work zone you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed throughout the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Increase your speed to get through quickly.
note: In work zones you must slow down, follow posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Workers, equipment, lane shifts, and uneven pavement can appear with little warning, so reducing speed and increasing following distance is essential for safety.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights frequently.,b:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.,c:Keep instrument panel lights very bright.,d:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.
note: At night you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate. This is called "overdriving your headlights" if you go too fast. Keeping speed low enough gives you time to see and react to hazards that appear in the lit area ahead.

question: Yellow centerlines on the road separate:
options: a:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.,b:Bike lanes from traffic lanes.,c:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,d:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. They mark the center of the roadway; solid and broken patterns tell you when passing is allowed. White lines, not yellow, separate lanes moving in the same direction, such as on one-way streets or multi-lane roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,b:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren while you are already in an intersection, you should continue through the intersection to clear it safely. Once you are completely out of the intersection, pull to the right side of the road and stop to yield the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At speeds of 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to crash if you:
options: a:Constantly change lanes to pass.,b:Match the general speed of other vehicles (stay within that range).,c:Drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,d:Drive much slower than surrounding traffic.
note: On high-speed roads, you are safest when you travel at a speed close to the general flow of traffic, as long as you stay within the posted speed limit. Large speed differences—whether you are much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic—increase the risk of rear-end and lane-change collisions.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is in bad condition it can cause:
options: a:Squealing brakes.,b:Vehicle control problems.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Bad suspension makes the vehicle bounce, lean, and handle poorly, which reduces traction and makes it harder to steer, brake, and keep control, especially in turns or during sudden maneuvers.

question: You should allow extra following distance when following:
options: a:A station wagon.,b:An emergency vehicle.,c:A small passenger car.,d:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (e.g., a large truck or bus).
note: You should leave extra following distance behind large or blocked‑view vehicles, like trucks or buses, because they may not see you in their mirrors and they limit your view of the road ahead, giving you less time to react.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Eating foods high in fat.,d:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing else will sober you up faster.

question: The best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation is to:
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle by scanning ahead, to the sides, and behind.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused only straight ahead of your car.
note: The safest way to avoid danger is to constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle so you can spot problems early and adjust your speed or position before a situation becomes hazardous.

question: Which statement best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They always assume they have the right-of-way.,b:They expect other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,d:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers assume other road users may make mistakes. They watch for possible hazards, leave space, and are ready to slow, stop, or change lanes to prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street you are entering moves to the left.
note: On a one‑way street, you may turn left onto another one‑way street only when traffic on the street you are entering is moving to the left. This ensures you will be turning into the correct lane and not driving against traffic. Always check for signs that may prohibit the turn, such as “No Left Turn” or “One Way” arrows pointing the opposite direction.

question: To make quick steering maneuvers safely, your hands should be:
options: a:At the bottom of the wheel only.,b:Next to each other at the top of the wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,d:On the top and bottom of the wheel.
note: For quick, controlled steering maneuvers, your hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around the 9‑and‑3 or 8‑and‑4 positions). This gives you maximum leverage and control, helps you steer smoothly, and reduces the chance of over‑steering or losing your grip in an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle moving in the same direction, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds have passed.,c:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to the right lane only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror. This visual check confirms you have enough space ahead of that vehicle so you do not cut it off or force it to brake suddenly when you move back into the lane.

question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days primarily to:
options: a:Warn others about poor weather.,b:Keep the engine warm.,c:Make your vehicle more visible to other drivers.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, you use your headlights mainly so other drivers can see you, not just so you can see the road. Low‑beam headlights make your vehicle more visible without causing glare or reflection that can happen with high beams in bad weather. Many states also require headlights whenever windshield wipers are in continuous use.

question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead when you:
options: a:Are being tailgated by another driver.,b:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,c:Are following a small passenger car.
note: When another driver is following too closely (tailgating), you should increase the space in front of your vehicle. A larger following distance gives you more time to brake gently and reduces the chance that a tailgater will hit you if you must slow down or stop. Avoid sudden braking and, when safe, allow the tailgater to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a row of parked vehicles you should:
options: a:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.,b:Expect all pedestrians and drivers to yield to you.,c:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: When passing parked vehicles, leave extra space and be ready for doors to open, cars to pull out, or pedestrians to step from between vehicles. Slowing slightly and covering the brake gives you time to react if something suddenly enters your lane.

question: If your vehicle starts skidding, you should:
options: a:Brake lightly and steer in the direction of the skid.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.,c:Stay off the brakes, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: In most skids, you should ease off the accelerator, avoid slamming on the brakes, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Braking hard usually makes a skid worse. In vehicles without ABS, you may need to pump the brakes gently if braking is necessary, but the first priority is to stay off the brakes and steer smoothly to regain control.

question: A flashing red light at an intersection is equivalent to:
options: a:A light about to turn green.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign — you must stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and traffic in or close to the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: As your speed increases, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Change lanes frequently to keep up with traffic.,c:Maintain the same following distance.,d:Look well ahead of your vehicle to allow time to react.
note: As speed increases, you need more time and distance to see hazards and stop safely. Looking well ahead helps you spot problems early so you can slow, change lanes, or stop smoothly instead of making sudden moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the maximum posted speed limit only when:
options: a:Road and weather conditions are ideal.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed under ideal conditions, not a required speed. In rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions, you must slow down to a speed that is safe for those conditions, even if it is below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot into the street, drivers should:
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.,b:Stop only if a pedestrian is standing on the sidewalk.,c:Assume pedestrians will yield and only stop if they block you.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area. This lets you look for and yield to pedestrians who have the right-of-way on the sidewalk. Only after the sidewalk is clear should you move forward to enter the street.

question: After having several beers, the effects will be reduced only by:
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Drinking several cups of coffee.,c:Waiting several hours.
note: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food. After drinking, you must wait long enough for your body to process the alcohol before driving.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline you may:
options: a:Change lanes only from the left lane.,b:Remain in your lane at all times,c:Cross the line to change lanes when it is safe.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,d:Proceed if you are going straight.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals. If needed, drivers should communicate with eye contact and proceed in turn.

question: How is driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic usually viewed?
options: a:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,b:Required by law.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.,d:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and attempt risky passes.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake, change lanes, or attempt risky passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and not block the normal, safe flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Left,b:Both left and right.,c:Only to the left.
note: Before entering an intersection, you should scan in all directions: left, right, ahead, and, if needed, behind. Most instructors teach: look left first (where the nearest cross‑traffic comes from), then right, then left again before you move. The key idea is to check both sides, not just one. Among the given choices, looking left is safer than only looking one way, but the best practice is to look both left and right.

question: Which of these statements about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are removed if you have one outside mirror on each side.,b:Blind spots can be seen by only using rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors and must check by turning your head. Large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger vehicles, so you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind them where the driver cannot see you.

question: At an intersection showing a flashing yellow light you should:
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.,b:Stop,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield if another road user is already in or entering the intersection.

question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:
options: a:Only when you see children present.,b:At all times.,c:Only during school hours.
note: School crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic at crossings. You must obey their instructions whenever they are on duty and giving directions, whether or not you see children and regardless of the exact time of day.

question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Slow down.,c:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent this is to slow down in wet conditions so your tires can maintain traction and channel water away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection you should:
options: a:Assume you have the right-of-way and proceed.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection before pedestrians move.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,d:Require pedestrians to wait for your vehicle.
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right‑of‑way, so you must yield and wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:
options: a:Enter as soon as the first two vehicles pass.,b:Honk and accelerate into traffic immediately.,c:Drive more slowly than traffic for the first 200 feet.,d:Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.
note: When pulling out from a curb, you must wait for a gap large enough to signal, pull out, and accelerate up to the speed of traffic without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: Large trucks commonly lose speed when:
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving on level roads.,c:Driving down long or steep hills.
note: Large, heavy trucks slow down when climbing long or steep hills because their weight makes it harder to maintain speed uphill. Expect them to lose speed on upgrades and give them extra space to avoid sudden lane changes or tailgating.

question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely only on the left side mirror.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,d:Change lanes without signaling.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal and check your mirrors, then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. This helps ensure there is no vehicle hidden beside you.

question: At a railroad crossing with gates down and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted.,b:Slow and crawl under the gate.,c:Drive around the lowered gates if you don't see a train.,d:Signal other drivers to go around.
note: At railroad crossings with gates down and lights flashing, you must stop before the gate and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised. It is both illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train, because trains can approach quickly and cannot stop in time.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning in heavy rain, you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,b:Drive at speeds for ideal conditions.,c:Slow down.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on a thin layer of water, causing a loss of steering and braking control. The most effective way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning is to slow down in wet conditions and avoid driving at high speeds, especially in heavy rain or standing water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Kentucky's point system, a driver age 18 or older faces a license suspension if they accumulate:
options: a:6 or more points in 1 year,b:12 or more points in a 2-year period,c:18 points in 3 years,d:10 points in 1 year
note: In Kentucky, drivers age 18 or older who accumulate 12 or more points within a two-year period may have their driving privileges suspended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Kentucky GDL laws, how many hours of practice driving must a permit holder age 16 or 17 complete and certify?
options: a:40 hours (including 10 at night),b:50 hours (including 10 at night),c:60 hours (including 10 at night),d:30 hours (including 5 at night)
note: Kentucky GDL law requires permit holders under age 18 to complete and document a minimum of 60 hours of practice driving, with at least 10 of those hours completed at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For permit holders under the age of 18 in Kentucky, between what nighttime hours is unsupervised driving prohibited?
options: a:10:00 PM to 5:00 AM,b:Midnight (12:00 AM) to 6:00 AM,c:11:00 PM to 6:00 AM,d:1:00 AM to 5:00 AM
note: Kentucky permit holders under age 18 are not allowed to operate a motor vehicle between the hours of midnight (12:00 AM) and 6:00 AM unless they have a valid exception or are accompanied by a parent/guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Kentucky's Child Passenger Safety law, a child must be secured in a booster seat if they are:
options: a:Under 6 years old and under 40 inches,b:Under 8 years old AND between 40 and 57 inches tall,c:Under 5 years old,d:Any height under age 10
note: Kentucky law requires children under 8 years of age who are between 40 and 57 inches tall to be properly secured in a belt-positioning booster seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a speed limit is not posted in Kentucky, what is the default speed limit on non-interstate state highways?
options: a:45 mph,b:55 mph,c:65 mph,d:35 mph
note: On Kentucky state highways where no speed limit is posted, the default speed limit is 55 miles per hour.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are involved in a traffic crash in Kentucky that results in property damage of $500 or more and is not investigated by police, you must file a written report within:
options: a:3 days,b:5 days,c:10 days,d:30 days
note: Kentucky law requires drivers to file a written Civilian Collision Report with the Kentucky State Police within 10 days of any crash resulting in property damage of $500 or more if the police did not investigate the scene.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum liability auto insurance coverage required for drivers in Kentucky under the split-limit rule?
note: Kentucky requires vehicle owners to maintain minimum liability coverage of 25/50/25: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 total per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.
